Hi Vanessa / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is positive on Redwood's performance. Procurement asked me to surface two items that are blockers for our Legal/Cloud Security review before we can sign the Order Form:

1) License boundary and residency: we need explicit language in the Order Form or an annex clarifying that any snapshots or runtime artifacts used for forensic or witness purposes are strictly read-only and stored within our VPC region.

2) Timebound audit / witness window: Silverline requires a defined temporary audit window (max 10 business days) during which a mutually-agreed witness can access a snapshot and run a limited validation script. We want to avoid any standing operator access or permanent escrow arrangements.

Attached is a draft SOW our security team sent earlier (SLH_VPC_SOW_v1.pdf) — it has some operational expectations. Can Redwood provide:
- A short proposed addendum clause for license and snapshot handling we can share with Legal,
- Confirmation on whether Redwood can create a cryptographic sealed snapshot deposited to an S3 bucket in our account for the witness run, and
- A rough estimate of any fees for witness facilitation / on-site support (if required).

Would appreciate a reply by EOD Thursday so we can keep the procurement timeline.

Subject: INTERNAL: suggested redlines for SLH VPC annex (license & audit window)

Team — quick internal note with proposed language and open points before we send a final version to Maria. This stays internal for now; do not forward until Vanessa approves.

Proposed clause (draft language):
"Snapshot Deposit and Witness Validation. Upon Customer's request and subject to Customer's provided S3 (or equivalent) storage account being properly configured, Provider will generate a read-only, cryptographically-signed snapshot of the deployment state (the 'Snapshot'), publish an immutable manifest including timestamp, SHA256 digest, operator identifier, and a random nonce, and deposit the Snapshot to the Customer's storage location. Provider will not retain any active copy of the Snapshot after deposit unless expressly agreed in writing.

Customer may request a single Witness Validation Window of up to ten (10) business days per twelve (12) month period (the 'Window'). During the Window, Provider will permit Customer (or a mutually-agreed third-party witness) to execute a predefined, containerized validation workload (provided by Customer) against the Snapshot within Customer's VPC. Provider shall not provide interactive operator console access as part of the standard Window. Any deviation (e.g., interactive support) shall be by exception and subject to additional fees.
"

Open questions / recommendations: 
- Limit to one Window per 12 months? Customer asked for a temporary window; restricting frequency reduces our long-term operational exposure. Recommend one Window / 12 months with ability to extend by mutual agreement.
- Liability / forensic access carveouts: add a line that the Snapshot and manifest are intended for validation only and Provider retains no rights to derivative works; Provider's liability for Snapshot integrity should be limited to standard warranty (we attest to digest and timestamp but do not guarantee forensic conclusions).
- Fees: recommend we hold to Vanessa's range but flag 'remote-first' for the run (remote witness verification supported by default; on-site subject to travel costs).

I'll inline these redlines into the attached draft and send a final copy to Maria after Vanessa signs off.

-Karthik

What we're offering (summary):
- Snapshot deposit: Provider will create a read-only, signed Snapshot (SHA256 + timestamp + operator id + nonce) and deposit to a Customer-managed S3 bucket. Redwood will not retain an operational copy after deposit.
- Witness Window: one (1) Witness Validation Window up to ten (10) business days per 12-month period. Default model is remote validation using a Customer-provided container; Provider will run the container in the Customer VPC. Interactive/operator console access is not included.
